niche_preference_profile: Prefers interfaces with strong, explicit information hierarchy; clear sectioning; readable labels; and obvious action states. Often favors light neutral backgrounds with dark text, subtle purple accents, soft outlined or lightly elevated cards, and calmer visual treatment. Repeatedly prefers organized list/card structures over decorative or fragmented layouts, explicit labels over implicit/icon-only cues, and balanced CTA presentation with visible primary actions and clear selection feedback. In some contexts also likes denser, information-rich layouts when the hierarchy remains structured and scannable.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers very clear hierarchy with prominent titles, section labels, grouped content, structured cards/lists, and easy-to-scan organization rather than flat, fragmented, or weakly structured layouts.

Most often prefers light neutral backgrounds with dark text and restrained accent colors, especially subtle purple; generally rejects harsher dark themes or overly saturated, high-contrast color treatments unless used in a clearly structured data-rich context.
Prefers balanced density: layouts that avoid clutter but also avoid wasteful emptiness, with breathable spacing, slimmer rows, and efficient use of space when content remains organized.
Prefers obvious, visible actions with strong CTA hierarchy, balanced button layouts, labeled actions, and clear primary/secondary distinction rather than hidden, weak, or ambiguous controls.
Prefers soft outlined or lightly elevated cards, moderate corner radius, restrained depth, and understated controls over heavy fills, exaggerated rounding, glowing treatments, or strong UI chrome.

Prefers high legibility, descriptive text labels, helper text, visible field labels, semantic badges, and explicit affordances instead of icon-only actions, placeholder-only labels, abbreviations, or low-contrast text.

Prefers cleaner compositions with fewer decorative elements, less visual noise, and focused content areas; rejects busy hero imagery, unnecessary icons, floating overlays, and attention-grabbing decoration that competes with the main task.
